units.translation: 117. ἐφέστιος Ἀσωπ〈οῖο〉: Asopus is a river of Thebes, having
22 The Boeotian river is confused with the Peloponnesian one; therefore H added καὶ ἕτερος after Θηβῶν
its springs in Araethyrea. He was struck by lightning by Zeus while pursuing him because he had abducted his daughter Aegina, as Callimachus (fr. 375 Schn.) also says. 〈...〉 to Aegina the city 〈...〉.

118-21a. Ἀργόθεν αὖ Ταλαός: from Argos the region, not the city. In the Great Ehoiai (Hesiod fr. 149 Rz.²) it is said that Melampus, being most dear to Apollo, went abroad and lodged with Polyphonte. When an ox was sacrificed to him, a serpent crawled up beside the victim, and the king's servants killed it; the king was angered, and Melampus took it and buried it, and its offspring, reared by him, licked his ears and breathed into him the art of prophecy. Therefore, when he was caught stealing the cattle of Iphiclus, he was bound, and when the house in which Iphiclus was was about to fall, he revealed it to the old woman among the servants, and for this favor he was released by Iphiclus. The story is clear.

b. 〈τῆς δ’ ἀμφί:〉 because of his brother Bias. Lg
c. 〈Αἰολίδης:〉 for he is the son of Amythaon, son of Cretheus, son of Aeolus, son of Hellen, son of Zeus. Lm(P)

d. σταθμοῖσιν ἐν Ἰφίκ〈λοιο〉: Iphiclus, son of Phylacus, son of Deioneus. The mother of Melampus is Dorippe, as Dieuchidas (fr. 9 M. IV 390) says. He also gives the reason for the name: that his mother, after giving birth to him, exposed him in a wooded place, and it happened that his feet were darkened by the sun, being unshaded.
124-29a. νεῖον ἀπ’ Ἀρκαδ〈ίης〉: with circumflex on the penult, meaning

“recently,” but with acute on the ultima, “the earth.” The sequence of thought is as follows: when he heard that the Argonauts were about to sail, having recently passed through Argos, along which road he was bringing the boar alive from Mount Erymanthus, where it grazed in the glens of Lampeia and Erymanthus, he came to Jason. Lampeia is a mountain of Arcadia, from which the river Erymanthus has its springs.
b. Λυγκήιον: from Lynceus, the king of Argos. But if it is Λυρκήιον, it must be understood from the mountain of Argos, from which the river Inachus flows down.
